FILED s444 from agent F (s443f) probes; PRE-EXISTING.  A registered bareword handle used as a WORD inside an ordinary expression emits a bare CL symbol -> unbound variable: `open(G,"<",...); print G . "x";` -> perl Gx (string "G" dot x), PCL dies "The variable G is unbound" (emission (p-. G "x")).  gen_leaf emits a handle name unquoted because the %p-fh-arg slots quote it themselves; outside such a slot nothing does.  Fix shape: outside a handle slot the Word is a STRING (strict-subs notwithstanding, principle 9).  This blocks running the close-G-dot inverse live (guarded on emitted shape today).

=== s449r (Opus round-7 agent R, 2026-08-29): ATTEMPTED, MEASURED, BACKED OUT.
The bug is re-probed and unchanged (five spellings crash: `my $s = G`,
`"x" . G`, `(G, 1)`, `G eq "G"`, `$s .= G`).  The attempt -- mark the Word
`_bareword_string` at handle_subcalls' registry exit and let
`_read_star_slot_bareword` claim it back -- FIXED all five and BROKE six
handle slots (chdir.t, closure.t, eval.t, flip.t and both shapes files), because
that helper reaches only ALL-CAPS names in a `*`-prototype funcall slot.
The finding: at that exit the token run for `close(G)` and for `my $s = G` are
the SAME (`G` alone), and for `pipe(READ, WRITE)` and `(G, 1)` the same again --
the discriminator is the PARENT slot, which the scan does not have.  Full
record, the six diff hunks and the three ways out: task #641.  Do not retry the
marker-plus-claim-back shape as written.
